chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
If the woman becomes pure before the rising of dawn, she prays Maghrib and the latter ʿIshaʾ. And if she becomes pure before the sun sets, she prays Zuhr and ʿAsr.

key_terms.الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ: the later night salat (prayer), meaning ʿIshaʾ
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman, here referring to the menstruating woman
key_terms.تَغِيبَ الشَّمْسُ: the sun sets, marking the end of the daytime prayer period
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: the rise of dawn, marking the end of the night prayer time

ai.seo_question: What prayers must a menstruating woman perform if she becomes pure before dawn or before sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a menstruating woman who regains ritual purity before the end of a prayer period. It states that if she becomes pure before dawn, she performs Maghrib and ʿIshaʾ, and if she becomes pure before sunset, she performs Zuhr and ʿAsr.
